name: Bodyweight Squat
steps: Stand with feet approximately shoulder-width apart and brace your trunk.
Bend at hips and knees to descend within a comfortable pain-free range.
Keep your whole foot in contact with the floor and knees moving in line with toes.
Stand tall by pushing through your feet.
summary: Practice sitting down and standing up with control.
startingPosition: Stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, arms relaxed or reaching forward for balance.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Sit your hips back and down as your knees bend, taking two to three seconds.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Push through your whole foot to stand back up, breathing out as you rise.

cues: Spread your weight across the whole foot.
Let your knees travel in the direction of your toes.
Only go as deep as you can control without pain.

name: Box Squat
steps: Place a sturdy chair or box behind you and stand just in front of it.
Sit back slowly until you lightly touch the seat.
Keep your chest tall and both feet flat.
Stand up by pressing through your feet without rocking forward.
summary: A squat with a seat behind you to guide depth and build confidence.
startingPosition: Stand a short step in front of a sturdy chair or box, feet about shoulder-width apart.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Reach your hips back toward the seat and lower slowly until you just touch it.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Press through your feet to stand tall without bouncing off the seat.

cues: Touch the seat lightly, do not sit down heavily.
Keep your feet flat the whole time.
Pick a seat height that feels controlled.

name: Goblet Squat
steps: Hold one dumbbell vertically at chest height with both hands.
Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Sit down between your hips while keeping the weight close to your chest.
Stand up by pushing through your whole foot.
mistakes: dumbbell drifting away from the chest
summary: A squat holding one dumbbell at your chest once bodyweight squats feel steady.
startingPosition: Stand tall holding a dumbbell vertically against your chest, elbows pointing down.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Sit down slowly, keeping the dumbbell close and your chest tall.

phases.label: Rising
phases.text: Drive through your feet to stand, breathing out on the way up.

cues: Hug the dumbbell close to your body.
Keep elbows pointing down.
Choose a weight you can control for every rep.

name: Push-Up
steps: Begin in a high plank with hands near shoulder-width.
Lower under control while keeping body aligned.
Press the floor away to return to plank.
summary: Build upper-body pushing strength one controlled rep at a time.
startingPosition: High plank: hands slightly wider than your shoulders, body in one line from head to heels.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor over about two seconds.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Press the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping your body in one line.

cues: Keep your elbows angled slightly back, not straight out.
Squeeze your glutes to keep hips level.
Stop the set when your form starts to change.

name: Incline Push-Up
steps: Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width on a stable raised surface.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the edge with control.
Press the surface away to return to the start.
easier: Use a higher surface, such as a wall
summary: A push-up with hands raised, so you can practice good form with less load.
startingPosition: Hands on a sturdy bench, table edge or counter; feet back so your body is one straight line.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the edge over about two seconds.

phases.label: Pressing
phases.text: Push the surface away until your arms are straight.

cues: Higher surface = easier; lower surface = harder.
Make sure the surface cannot slide or tip.
Keep your body in one line.

name: Supported Dumbbell Row
steps: Brace one hand on a stable support.
Keep back controlled, pull dumbbell toward hip.
Lower slowly with control.
summary: Train your upper back with one hand supported for stability.
startingPosition: One hand and knee (or just one hand) on a bench or sturdy chair, dumbbell in the other hand, back long and flat.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Draw your elbow back toward your hip, keeping your chest facing the floor.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower the dumbbell slowly until your arm is straight again.

cues: Think elbow to hip, not hand to shoulder.
Keep your shoulders level.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.

name: Seated Band Row
steps: Sit tall with legs extended and loop the band around your feet.
Hold one end in each hand with arms straight.
Pull your elbows back toward your ribs, gently drawing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
summary: An upper-back pull you can do anywhere with a resistance band.
startingPosition: Seated on the floor, legs straight, band looped around your feet, arms reaching forward.

phases.label: Pulling
phases.text: Draw your elbows back past your ribs while sitting tall.

phases.label: Returning
phases.text: Let your arms extend slowly against the band's pull.

cues: Sit tall the whole time.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Control the band on the way back.

name: Prone Y Raise
steps: Lie face down with your arms overhead in a Y shape, thumbs pointing up.
Rest your forehead on a folded towel.
Lift your arms a few centimetres off the floor by drawing your shoulder blades back and down.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly.
mistakes: arching the lower back to lift higher
summary: A no-equipment upper-back exercise when you have no dumbbell or band.
startingPosition: Face down on a mat, arms overhead in a Y, forehead resting on a folded towel.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Raise both arms slightly by drawing your shoulder blades back and down.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower your arms to the floor over two seconds.

cues: Small lift, big focus on the upper back.
Keep your neck relaxed and long.
Breathe steadily.

name: Hip Hinge
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hands on your hips.
Push your hips back, letting your torso tip forward as one unit.
Keep your back long; stop when you feel a stretch in the back of your thighs.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
summary: Learn to bend from the hips, the basis for lifting things safely off the floor.
startingPosition: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, a slight bend in the knees, hands on your hips.

phases.label: Hinging
phases.text: Send your hips back slowly while your chest tips forward and your back stays long.

phases.label: Standing
phases.text: Squeeze your glutes and bring your hips forward to stand tall.

cues: Imagine closing a car door with your hips.
Keep the knee bend small and steady.
Finish tall, without leaning back.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
With soft knees, push your hips back and slide the weights down along your legs.
Keep the dumbbells close and your back long; stop at a comfortable stretch.
Squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
mistakes: weights drifting away from the legs
going lower than you can control
summary: A loaded hip hinge once the bodyweight version feels natural.
startingPosition: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand against the front of your thighs.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Hinge at the hips and slide the dumbbells down your legs over two to three seconds.

phases.label: Standing
phases.text: Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

cues: Dumbbells stay close to your legs.
Range ends where your back starts to round.
Choose a load you can control for every rep.

name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Brace lightly and press through your heels to lift your hips.
Pause when your body forms a line from shoulders to knees.
Lower slowly to the floor.
mistakes: over-arching the lower back at the top
summary: A floor-based way to practice using your glutes.
startingPosition: On your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.

phases.label: Lifting
phases.text: Press through your heels to raise your hips until shoulders, hips and knees line up.

phases.label: Lowering
phases.text: Lower your hips back to the floor over two seconds.

cues: Push through your heels.
Stop at a straight line; do not over-arch.
Pause for a breath at the top.

name: Front Plank
steps: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back to form a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your trunk and breathe steadily.
Hold for the target time, then lower your knees to rest.
easier: Plank from your knees or with forearms on a bench
summary: Practice holding your trunk steady. Quality matters more than time.
startingPosition: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, legs extended behind you.

phases.label: Holding
phases.text: Keep a straight line from head to heels and breathe slowly; stop when your hips start to drop.

cues: Shaking is normal; sagging is the signal to stop.
Squeeze your glutes gently.
Shorter, better holds beat long, sloppy ones.
